meta.subject: Phnom Penh, Cambodia
meta.quote_rule: Each quote is verbatim from the source page text; checked by script against the fetched text on compile.
notes: name_th_roman is the researcher's Royal Thai General System reading of the Thai script; name_km_roman is from the source where one was shown and otherwise the researcher's UNGEGN-style reading. Neither has been reviewed by a native reader.

timeline.year_note: date in tradition; first recorded about a century after
timeline.text_en: Tradition dates the founding of Phnom Penh to 1372. Penh, a wealthy woman living at Chaktomuk, finds a floating koki tree holding four Buddha statues and one of Vishnu, and has a hill raised for them.
timeline.quote: According to legend, in 1372, a wealthy old lady named "Penh"

also.quote: credited as having founded Phnom Penh, the capital of Cambodia, in 1372 AD
First recorded a century after it is said to have taken place

timeline.year_note: Wikipedia pages give 1397, 1400, 1431, 1432 and 1434 for the move
timeline.text_en: Ponhea Yat leaves Angkor and settles at Chaktomuk, where Phnom Penh stands. English Wikipedia gives 1434 for Phnom Penh succeeding Angkor Thom as the capital.
timeline.quote: succeeded Angkor Thom as the national capital in 1434 following the fall of Angkor

also.quote: fled to Chaktomuk (now part of "Phnom Penh")

timeline.text_en: King Ang Chan I moved the capital from Chaktomuk to Longvek (Lovek) in 1529; Longvek was the capital until 1594. Oudong was the royal capital from 1618 until 1866.
timeline.quote: moved the capital city from Chaktomuk to Longvek in 1529

also.quote: capital of the Kingdom of Cambodia from 1529 to 1594
the royal capital of Cambodia for 250 years

timeline.text_en: King Norodom signed a treaty on 11 August 1863 that placed Cambodia under a French protectorate. A resident general was housed in Phnom Penh.
timeline.quote: Norodom signed a treaty acknowledging a French protectorate over his kingdom

timeline.year_note: Wikipedia gives 1865 (Phnom Penh page), 1866 (Oudong and Thai pages) and 1867 (Central Market page) for the capital's re-establishment
timeline.text_en: King Norodom left Oudong with his court for Phnom Penh. The Royal Palace was built between 1866 and 1870.
timeline.quote: taking his royal court along with him to the current capital, Phnom Penh

also.quote: constructed by King Norodom between 1866 and 1870

timeline.text_en: The Central Market (Phsar Thmei), designed by city architect Jean Desbois, was inaugurated by King Sisowath Monivong in September 1937. It has a 26-metre central dome.
timeline.quote: the market was inaugurated by King Sisowath Monivong in September 1937

also.quote: has a 26-metre high central dome

timeline.text_en: Cambodia celebrated independence from France on 9 November 1953.
timeline.quote: independence day was celebrated on 9 November 1953

timeline.text_en: The Independence Monument, 37 metres tall and designed by Vann Molyvann, was built at the crossing of Norodom and Sihanouk boulevards.
timeline.quote: was built in 1958 to memorialise Cambodia's independence from France in 1953

also.quote: It stands 37 metres tall

timeline.year_note: Vann Molyvann was named chief national architect in 1956
timeline.text_en: The National Sports Complex with the Olympic Stadium, designed by Vann Molyvann, was completed in 1964. The stadium has never hosted an Olympic Games.
timeline.quote: Construction on the National Sports Complex started in 1963 and was completed in 1964

also.quote: nominated chief national architect by the king himself in 1956
appointed by Norodom Sihanouk to reshape and modernise Cambodia

timeline.text_en: The Khmer Rouge took Phnom Penh on 17 April 1975 and ordered the evacuation of the city. The population was 2 to 3 million, most of them refugees from the fighting.
timeline.quote: The Khmer Rouge ordered the evacuation of Phnom Penh, emptying the city

also.quote: by the Khmer Rouge on 17 April 1975
By 1975, the population was 2–3 million

timeline.year_note: Tuol Sleng (S-21); death toll estimates differ by source
timeline.text_en: Under Democratic Kampuchea the former Tuol Svay Prey school in Phnom Penh ran as Security Prison 21 (S-21). The museum states that 15,000 to 20,000 people were imprisoned there and that 12 people were found alive at the site in January 1979. The ECCC states that over a million people were killed or perished in Democratic Kampuchea; English Wikipedia gives approximately 2 million deaths.
timeline.quote: 15,000 – 20,000 people were imprisoned from all parts of Cambodia

also.quote: 12 people who had escaped execution, including 4 children, were found
Over a million people were killed or perished in Democratic Kampuchea
approximately 2 million people from 1975 to 1979

timeline.text_en: Vietnamese forces (PAVN) entered Phnom Penh with members of the KUFNS on 7 January 1979.
timeline.quote: the PAVN entered Phnom Penh along with members of the KUFNS

timeline.text_en: The Paris Peace Agreements were signed on 23 October 1991. UNTAC administered Cambodia in 1992–93 and ran the elections.

also.quote: a United Nations administrative and peacekeeping operation in Cambodia in 1992–93

timeline.year_note: agreement signed 6 June 2003; Duch convicted 26 July 2010
timeline.text_en: The Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia (ECCC), set up by agreement between the Cambodian government and the UN, held investigations and trials in Phnom Penh. It convicted Kaing Guek Eav (Duch), the head of S-21, on 26 July 2010. It concluded in December 2022 with three convictions.
timeline.quote: Investigations and court proceedings took place between 2006 and 2022.

also.quote: On 26 July 2010, the Extraordinary Chambers in the Courts of Cambodia convicted
signed on 6 June 2003
the tribunal concluded in December 2022, with three convictions in all

timeline.text_en: Development of Koh Pich (Diamond Island), an island in the Bassac River near Chaktomuk, began in 2006.
timeline.quote: Development began in 2006, when OCIC, the developer of Koh Pich

timeline.text_en: Techo International Airport, 19 km south of Phnom Penh in Kandal Province, became operational on 9 September 2025 and replaced Phnom Penh International Airport as the city's main airport.
timeline.quote: the first phase was operational on 9 September 2025

also.quote: An official inauguration ceremony was held on 20 October 2025

legends.title_en: Lady Penh and the koki tree
legends.title_km: ដូនពេញ និងដើមគគី
legends.title_th: ยายเพ็ญและต้นตะเคียน
legends.title_basis: composed from sourced terms: ដូនពេញ and ដើមគគី (km Wat Phnom page), ยายเพ็ญ and ต้นตะเคียน (th Penh page)
legends.story_en: Penh, a wealthy woman living at Chaktomuk, sees a koki tree floating in the river and has it pulled ashore. Inside are four Buddha statues and one of Vishnu. She has a hill raised on the west bank of the Tonlé Sap and puts a shrine on it. The hill becomes Wat Phnom, and the city is called Phnom Penh, Penh's hill.
legends.quote: Penh raised a hill on the west bank of the Tonle Sap River

also.quote: พบว่ามีพระพุทธรูปและเทวรูปอยู่ในโพรงต้นตะเคียน
ត្រូវបានប្រសិទ្ធនាម តាមឈ្មោះ លោកយាយ ដូនពេញ
four Buddha statues made of bronze, brass and one made of marble

legends.note: The legend was first recorded about a century after 1372 (English Wikipedia, Phnom Penh). The Thai Wat Phnom page gives 1373 for construction.

legends.title_basis: ចតុមុខ from km Phnom Penh page; จตุมุข from th Phnom Penh page
legends.story_en: Chaktomuk, 'four faces', is the name of the place where the Upper and Lower Mekong, the Tonlé Sap and the Bassac meet in front of Phnom Penh. The name alludes to Brahma. King Ponhea Yat gave the city the name Krong Chaktomuk.
legends.place: Confluence of the Mekong, Tonlé Sap and Bassac, Phnom Penh

also.quote: the junction of four rivers
Chaktomuk (an allusion to Brahma)
เมืองที่มีสี่ใบหน้า

legends.title_en: The Tonlé Sap reverses its flow
legends.title_basis: Wikidata labels and km/th Wikipedia titles for Tonlé Sap
legends.story_en: The 115-kilometre Tonlé Sap River flows six months a year from the Mekong toward the lake and six months a year in the opposite direction. Inflow to the lake starts in May or June and ends in October or November, and in November the lake reaches its maximum size. The change of direction is what Bon Om Touk marks.
legends.place: Tonlé Sap River at Phnom Penh
legends.quote: six months a year in the opposite direction

also.quote: Inflow starts in May or June
change in flow of the Tonlé Sap River

legends.title_en: The nāga's tooth and the water festival
legends.title_km: បុណ្យអុំទូក
legends.title_basis: festival name Bon Om Touk, from the en Bon Om Touk page and Wikidata
legends.story_en: In one account the water celebrations honour a tooth lost in the depths by a nāga whose daughter married a Buddhist Indian prince and founded the kingdom of Cambodia. After two days of racing, the canoes come together to urge the nāga to spit the swelling waters of the Tonlé Sap toward the sea. That tells the master of the water to return to the depths, and it marks the end of the rainy season.
legends.place: Tonlé Sap and the Sisowath Quay riverfront, Phnom Penh
legends.quote: a tooth lost in the depths by a nāga

also.quote: boat races along the Sisowath Quay riverfront

legends.title_km: ព្រះថោង និងនាងនាគ
legends.title_th: ตำนานพระทอง-นางนาค
legends.title_basis: ព្រះថោង from km Preah Thong page, នាងនាគ from km Soma page; th title is the th Wikipedia article title
legends.story_en: A foreign Brahmin prince, Preah Thong, marries the nāga princess Neang Neak and founds Funan, the first kingdom of Cambodia. Chinese accounts record a similar tradition of a foreign prince, Hun-tian, who marries the local ruler Liu-ye. Much of Khmer wedding custom is traced to this marriage, and the nāga became part of Khmer iconography.
legends.place: Funan; a national foundation myth, not tied to a Phnom Penh site in the sources
legends.quote: Preah Thong married a Nāga princess Neang Neak

also.quote: can be traced back to the marriage of Preah Thong and Neang Neak
the serpent (Nāga) became an important part of Khmer iconography

legends.title_km: ព្រះគោ ព្រះកែវ
legends.title_th: พระโค พระแก้ว
legends.title_basis: en Wikipedia lead (km); th Wikipedia article title
legends.story_en: Two brothers are born in Cambodia: Preah Ko, an ox with divine power whose belly holds precious objects, and Preah Keo, a man. They bring peace and prosperity to the place where they live. One reading takes the tale as an account of the treasures lost when Lovek fell in 1594.
legends.quote: Preah Ko possessed divine power, and his belly contained precious and valuable objects

also.quote: particularly the fall of Lovek in 1594

legends.title_basis: en Wikipedia lead; no Thai source found
legends.story_en: A neak ta is an ancestral or tutelary spirit that watches over people, places and things while they are shown respect. The cult comes before Hinduism and Buddhism in Cambodia and has no priesthood. At Wat Phnom a small shrine to Lady Penh stands at the southwest corner of the temple, and the English Wikipedia page names a hermitage on the hill Neak Ta Preah Chao.
legends.quote: ancestral or tutelary deity, believed locally to watch over people, places, and things

also.quote: it preceded both Hinduism and Buddhism in Cambodia
a small shrine dedicated to Lady Penh
which Cambodians today call Neak Ta Preah Chao

legends.title_km: ព្រះអង្គដងកើ
legends.title_basis: Khmer spelling from Hello Angkor; no Thai source found
legends.story_en: A shrine near the Royal Palace on Sisowath Quay holds a black-lacquered statue in the style of a 12th to 13th century Avalokiteshvara. Worshippers treat it as an ancestral spirit, tied to a local legend about the flagpole there. A second shrine to the north holds three deities: Lokta Dambang Dek, Lokta Krahorm and Lokta Preah Chao.
legends.place: Sisowath Quay near the Royal Palace, Daun Penh
legends.quote: it is actually an ancestral spirit that people come here to worship

also.quote: a local legend surrounding the flagpole here

legends.note: The flagpole legend itself is not in the source. The name 'Preah Ang Dangkar' appears in no source found; the spelling in Hello Angkor is Dorngkeu. English Wikipedia's 'Preah Ang Chek Preah Ang Chorm shrine' is in Siem Reap, not Phnom Penh. Hello Angkor is a private site.

people.one_line_en: Wealthy woman credited with founding Phnom Penh in 1372, according to tradition.
people.quote: credited as having founded Phnom Penh, the capital of Cambodia, in 1372 AD

people.one_line_en: Khmer king who moved the court from Angkor to Chaktomuk, the site of Phnom Penh, and ordered six Buddhist monasteries built around the city.
people.quote: fled to Chaktomuk (now part of "Phnom Penh")

also.quote: he also ordered the construction of six Buddhist monasteries around the city

people.name_km: ព្រះនរោត្តម
people.name_th: พระบาทสมเด็จพระนโรดม บรมรามเทวาวตาร
people.name_th_roman: Phra Bat Somdet Phra Narodom Boromramathewawatan
people.one_line_en: King who signed the 1863 protectorate treaty with France and moved his court to Phnom Penh, where the Royal Palace was built in 1866–1870.
people.quote: was King of Cambodia from 19 October 1860 until his death in 1904

also.quote: in 1863 he signed a treaty with the French

people.name_km: នរោត្ដម សីហនុ
people.name_th: พระบาทสมเด็จพระนโรดม สีหนุ
people.name_th_roman: Phra Bat Somdet Phra Narodom Sihanu
people.one_line_en: King, Chief of State and Prime Minister; secured independence from France in 1953 and sought a new style of architecture for Phnom Penh in the 1950s and 1960s.
people.quote: he secured Cambodian independence from France in 1953

also.quote: King Sihanouk was eager to present a new style of architecture

people.name_km: វណ្ណ មូលីវណ្ណ
people.name_th: วัณณ์ โมลีวัณณ์

people.quote: credited with modernising the nation's capital Phnom Penh
people.name_km_alt: វណ្ណ ម៉ូលីវណ្ណ (en Wikipedia lead spelling)

people.name_km: ស៊ីន ស៊ីសាមុត
people.name_th: สิน ศรีสมุทร
people.one_line_en: Singer-songwriter of the Phnom Penh music scene of the 1950s to 1970s; died under the Khmer Rouge in unclear circumstances.
people.quote: Widely considered the "King of Khmer Music"

also.quote: Sisamouth died during the Khmer Rouge regime under circumstances that are unclear

people.name_km: រស់ សេរីសុទ្ធា
people.name_th: รส สิริสุทธา
people.one_line_en: Singer; Sihanouk gave her the title 'Queen with the Golden Voice'. She disappeared under the Khmer Rouge.
people.quote: the most prominent female artist in the Cambodian rock scene

also.quote: Queen with the Golden Voice

people.name_th_source: Wikidata label Q2982405 (no th Wikipedia article)

people.one_line_en: Singer and songwriter with western rock and soul influences; recorded with Sinn Sisamouth from 1966. Her fate under the Khmer Rouge is unknown.
people.quote: She disappeared during the Khmer Rouge genocide and her fate is unknown

people.name_km: នរោត្តម បុប្ផាទេវី
people.name_th: สมเด็จพระเรียมนโรดม บุปผาเทวี
people.name_th_roman: Somdet Phra Riam Narodom Buppha Thewi
people.one_line_en: Prima ballerina and director of the Royal Ballet of Cambodia; later Minister of Culture and Fine Arts.
people.quote: dancer, director of the Royal Ballet of Cambodia, senator

also.quote: At the age of 18, she was granted the title of prima ballerina

people.name_km: ប៉ាន់ រិទ្ធី

also.quote: S-21: The Khmer Rouge Killing Machine

also.quote: stayed behind in Cambodia to cover the fall of the capital Phnom Penh

people.one_line_en: Mechanic in Phnom Penh, evacuated on 17 April 1975, held at S-21 from 28 October 1978; one of very few survivors; testified at the ECCC in 2009.
people.quote: was one of very few survivors of S-21

also.quote: was 79 years old in 2009, when he testified

people.one_line_en: Executive director of the Documentation Center of Cambodia (DC-Cam) since 1995; born in Phnom Penh and separated from his family during the evacuation of 17 April 1975.
people.quote: executive director of the Documentation Center of Cambodia

sites.quote: serves as the official royal residence of the King of Cambodia

sites.name_km: សារមន្ទីរជាតិ
sites.name_th: พิพิธภัณฑสถานแห่งชาติกัมพูชา

sites.quote: one of the world's largest collections of Khmer art

also.quote: Wat Phnom has a total height of 46 meters

sites.quote: one of the five oldest pagodas in Phnom Penh

sites.why_en: One of the five ancient pagodas of Phnom Penh, built in 1442 as a place to keep the Tripitaka and as a meeting place for Khmer and Sri Lankan monks; named for that meeting.
sites.quote: one of the five ancient pagodas in Phnom Penh

also.quote: ពីព្រោះកាលពីមុន ផ្សារនេះធ្លាប់លក់ទំនិញនាំចូលពីប្រទេសរុស្ស៊ី

sites.quote: was originally opened as La salle de conférence Chaktomuk

culture.name_en: Royal Ballet of Cambodia (Khmer classical dance)
culture.name_km: របាំព្រះរាជទ្រព្យ
culture.what_en: Court dance tied to the Khmer court for over a thousand years; inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List in 2008 (proclaimed 2003). Four character types: Neang (woman), Neayrong (man), Yeak (giant) and Sva (monkey). Gestures and poses evoke emotions from fear and rage to love and joy; an orchestra plays and a female chorus comments on the plot. The Khmer Rouge eliminated almost all master dancers and musicians; troupes re-emerged after 1979.
culture.quote: has been closely associated with the Khmer court for over one thousand years

also.quote: Four distinct character types exist in the classical repertory
Inscribed in 2008 ( 3.COM ) on the Representative List
Registration Date 07 November, 2003

kbach_gestures.note: Ministry of Culture and Fine Arts names the four basic hand gestures. Hand gestures are called kbach (English Wikipedia).
kbach_gestures.quote: “Sprout” means birth, “Leaf” means evolution, “Flower” means growth

culture.note: No dedicated Thai article found; th Wikipedia has a general page on Cambodian dance, นาฏศิลป์ในประเทศกัมพูชา.

culture.name_km: ល្ខោនស្បែកធំ
culture.what_en: Shadow theatre with two-metre leather puppets, staged at night in front of a white screen and a fire or projectors; performances come from the Reamker and can last several nights, using up to 160 puppets. Inscribed on the UNESCO Representative List in 2008 (proclaimed 2005).
culture.quote: Inspired from the Reamker, the Khmer version of the Ramayana

also.quote: may last several nights and require up to 160 puppets for a single presentation
Inscribed in 2008 ( 3.COM ) on the Representative List

culture.note: Khmer shadow theatre in general is ល្ខោនណាំងស្បែក (en Wikipedia); Sbek Thom is the large-puppet genre.

culture.name_km: ចាប៉ីដងវែង
culture.what_en: Musical tradition in which a performer sings and plays the chapei, a lute, with texts that range from teaching to social commentary and satire. Inscribed on the UNESCO list of intangible heritage in need of urgent safeguarding in 2016.
culture.quote: the chapei (a type of lute often played at cultural festivals) accompanied by singing

also.quote: Inscribed in 2016 ( 11.COM )
List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in Need of Urgent Safeguarding

culture.what_en: Masked dance drama performed by men with a traditional orchestra and recitation. The Wat Svay Andet form, about 10 km east of Phnom Penh on the Mekong, is performed to propitiate the Neak Ta, and was inscribed in 2018 on the UNESCO list in need of urgent safeguarding.
culture.quote: performed by men wearing masks to the accompaniment of a traditional orchestra

also.quote: Inscribed in 2018 ( 13.COM )
List of Intangible Cultural Heritage in Need of Urgent Safeguarding
The specific aim is to propitiate the Neak Ta

culture.name_en: Bon Om Touk (Water and Moon Festival)
culture.name_km: បុណ្យអុំទូក
culture.what_en: Three-day festival held in late October or early November, on the 14th and 15th days of the waxing moon and the 1st day of the waning moon of the month of Kadek, at the end of the monsoon season. It marks the change in flow of the Tonlé Sap River. Boat races run along the Sisowath Quay riverfront, with fireworks and evening concerts.
culture.quote: 14th and 15th of the waxing moon and the 1st of the waning moon

also.quote: celebrated in late October or early November
boat races along the Sisowath Quay riverfront

culture.date_rule: 14th–15th of the waxing moon and 1st of the waning moon of Kadek (Khmer lunar month); the Gregorian date moves each year

culture.name_km: បុណ្យភ្ជុំបិណ្ឌ
culture.name_th: บุญภชุมบิณฑ์
culture.what_en: 15-day religious festival ending on the 15th day of the tenth month of the Khmer calendar, at the end of Buddhist Lent. Many Cambodians pay respects to deceased relatives of up to seven generations and make food offerings through monks.

also.quote: pay their respects to deceased relatives of up to seven generations

culture.name_km: បុណ្យចូលឆ្នាំខ្មែរ
culture.what_en: Three-day public holiday marking the solar new year at the end of the harvest season, with days named Moha Sangkrant and others; New Year's Day usually falls on 13 or 14 April.
culture.quote: which usually falls on 13 April or 14 April

also.quote: A three-day public holiday in the country

culture.what_en: Music scene based in Phnom Penh that combined traditional Cambodian music with rock and pop from imported records. The Khmer Rouge ended it in 1975, and many musicians disappeared or were executed. Sinn Sisamouth, Ros Serey Sothea and Pen Ran belonged to it.
culture.quote: a thriving and prolific music scene based in Phnom Penh

also.quote: many of its musicians disappeared or were executed during the ensuing Cambodian genocide

culture.note: No Khmer or Thai article title found for the genre.

culture.name_km: អក្សរខ្មែរ
culture.what_en: Abugida used to write Khmer, the official language and script under Article 5 of the constitution. Modern Khmer uses 33 of the original 35 consonant characters, and the script also writes Pali in Buddhist liturgy.
culture.quote: The official language and script is Khmer.

also.quote: Originally there were 35 consonant characters, but modern Khmer uses only 33
to write Pali in the Buddhist liturgy of Cambodia and Thailand

culture.name_km: ព្រះពុទ្ធសាសនា
culture.name_th: ศาสนาพุทธในประเทศกัมพูชา
culture.what_en: Article 43 of the constitution makes Buddhism the religion of the State. Theravada Buddhism has been the state religion since the 13th century except during the Khmer Rouge period; English Wikipedia gives 97.1 percent of the population as Buddhist in 2019.
culture.quote: Buddhism shall be the religion of the State.

also.quote: Theravada Buddhism has been the Cambodian state religion since the 13th century
97.1 percent of the population are Buddhists

food.what_en: Rice-noodle soup in a clear pork-bone broth with toppings, served mostly at breakfast. The Phnom Penh version carries the most toppings, which may include ground pork, sliced pork loin, pork belly, pork ribs, blood jelly, liver, prawns or shrimp.
food.phnom_penh_tie: specific: the Phnom Penh version is named in the source
food.quote: Kuyteav Phnom Penh may contain some or all of the following toppings

also.quote: a Cambodian noodle soup consisting of rice noodles with pork stock and toppings

food.what_en: Lightly fermented rice noodles served as a breakfast dish with fish-based or coconut-based gravy; the Siem Reap and samlor proher versions use kroeung, freshwater fish and prahok.
food.quote: lightly fermented Cambodian rice noodles and a breakfast noodle dish
food.name_en_note: Wikipedia spells it 'num banhchok'; the brief used 'nom banh chok'.

food.name_km: អាម៉ុកត្រី
food.what_en: Steamed fish curry with a mousse-like consistency, cooked in a banana-leaf container with kroeung, coconut cream and eggs and served with rice. It is considered one of Cambodia's national dishes.
food.quote: a Khmer steamed fish curry (amok) with a mousse-like consistency

food.name_km: បាយសាច់ជ្រូក
food.what_en: Rice with thin cuts of pork marinated in palm sugar, garlic, coconut milk and fish sauce, kept warm over a grill or coals; a common breakfast dish with chicken broth, radish and fried onion.
food.quote: a Cambodian pork and rice dish

food.what_en: Beef cut into small cubes, marinated in fish, soy and oyster sauce and sauteed with onion and pepper, served on lettuce with tomato and cucumber. The source says the dish began in Saigon and is both Vietnamese and Cambodian.
food.quote: a Vietnamese and Cambodian dish that consists of beef

food.what_en: Short baguette with a thin crisp crust, split and filled with pâté, pork, meatballs or beef, pickled carrot and herbs. Baguettes came to Cambodia from the French during the protectorate.
food.quote: Baguettes were adopted into Cambodian cuisine from the French

food.what_en: Salted, fermented fish paste, usually of mudfish, used as a seasoning in soups and sauces. Fermentation lasts about one month.
food.quote: a salted and fermented fish paste

also.quote: Fermentation typically lasts about one month

food.what_en: Glutinous rice mixed with beans, coconut milk, grated coconut and palm sugar and roasted in a bamboo tube over a fire for about 90 minutes. It is often eaten at Chinese and Khmer New Year.
food.quote: In Cambodia, sticky rice in bamboo is called kralan

also.quote: Kralan is often eaten at Chinese and Khmer New Year

food.name_th_note: ข้าวหลาม is the Thai name for the same dish.

food.what_en: Black pepper grown in Kampot Province, a certified geographical indication in Cambodia since 2010 and in the European Union since 2016. It is crushed over kuy teav.
food.phnom_penh_tie: none stated in the source; Kampot is a province
food.quote: a cultivar of black pepper (Piper nigrum) grown and produced in Cambodia

also.quote: certified geographical indication (GI) product in Cambodia (since 2010)
crushed black Kampot pepper

food.name_th: น้ำตาลปี๊บ
food.what_en: Sweetener from palm sap, used in marinades for bai sach chrouk, in kralan and in stir-fries. Kampong Speu palm sugar holds a geographical indication in Cambodia and in the European Union.
food.quote: have been granted Geographical Indications in Cambodia

also.quote: marinated in palm sugar, garlic, coconut milk, and fish sauce

food.name_th_note: The Thai article is about palm sugar in general.

numbers.quote: Phnom Penh had the highest population with 2,281,951

also.quote: Phnom Penh has the highest population at 2,129,371

numbers.note: National Institute of Statistics. The provisional report gave 2,129,371; English Wikipedia's text uses the provisional figure and its infobox gives 2,352,851. Share of Cambodia: 14.7 percent. Enumeration night 3 March 2019.

numbers.quote: Phnom Penh has the highest population density at 3,361 persons per km2
an autonomous municipality of area 678.46 square kilometres

also.quote: subdivided into 14 administrative divisions called khans

numbers.note: Counted from the Phnom Penh table of the NIS final census report (105 sangkat rows under 14 khans).

numbers.quote: Founded in 1372, Phnom Penh succeeded Angkor Thom

numbers.note: Other pages in the same encyclopedia give 1432 to 1505.

numbers.quote: It has been the national capital since 1865

also.quote: Phnom Penh is the capital city of the Kingdom of Cambodia.

numbers.quote: Phnom Penh is at 11.89 metres (39 ft)
numbers.note: The page text adds 'above the river'; the infobox lists elevation 11.89 m.

also.quote: joined on the right bank by the river and lake system Tonlé Sap

numbers.value: Lake inflow from May or June to October or November; the river runs each way about six months a year
numbers.quote: Inflow starts in May or June

also.quote: ends in October or November
six months a year in the opposite direction

numbers.label_en: Khmer Rouge rule over Phnom Penh
numbers.quote: by the Khmer Rouge on 17 April 1975

also.quote: the PAVN entered Phnom Penh along with members of the KUFNS

numbers.label_en: Deaths in Democratic Kampuchea, ECCC statement
numbers.quote: Over a million people were killed or perished in Democratic Kampuchea

also.quote: approximately 2 million people from 1975 to 1979
between 1.671 million and 1.871 million Cambodians died

numbers.note: Estimates differ: ECCC over 1 million; Kiernan 1.671–1.871 million; Sliwinski slightly under 2 million; English Wikipedia lead approximately 2 million (around 25 percent of the 1975 population).

numbers.quote: 15,000 – 20,000 people were imprisoned from all parts of Cambodia

also.quote: 12 people who had escaped execution, including 4 children, were found
